name: SeqWins Display
author: destinyexpress

sections.description:
A SeqWins walks somebody through a process one step at a time: a screenshot with the important part marked, a short instruction, and a button to the page where they do it. You make SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com. SeqWins Display shows them on your own WordPress website, records how your visitors get on, and tells you about it.

How it works

  1. In wp-admin, go to SeqWins Display and press Connect to SeqWins.
  2. Sign in to angelsponsoring.com and approve your website. You are brought straight back.
  3. Tick the SeqWins you want on this website and press Copy.

Made on angelsponsoring.com

SeqWins are made on angelsponsoring.com: screen capture, recording and editing all happen there, and this plugin has none of it. Press Create a SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com on the SeqWins screen, make and save it there, then come back to wp-admin: it is marked New and ready to copy.

Each SeqWins is copied to your website, screenshots and all, so it loads from your own server with nothing waiting on another site. A SeqWins copied to your website is always shown, even while angelsponsoring.com can’t be reached or after you disconnect.

Live SeqWins

Live SeqWins is the SeqWins browser extension, on the Chrome Web Store (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera) and as a signed Firefox file on angelsponsoring.com. A SeqWins recorded with it can also guide its viewers on the website the steps are on: viewers whose browser has it see Guide me on the website itself, which opens the SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com at the step they have reached, where Live SeqWins takes over with one press. Everyone else follows the screenshots on your page.

Place a SeqWins anywhere

Whole, or as a card — its title, a line of its introduction, how many steps and its first screenshot, with a Start button that opens the whole SeqWins in its place (or goes to a page you choose).

  • New page with it: one press on the SeqWins or Library screen makes a draft page holding it.
  • Block: “SeqWins”, in the block editor’s Embeds group (whole or card).
  • Shortcode: [seqwins_display id="123"], [seqwins_display id="123" view="card"].
  • WPBakery: a “SeqWins” element in the Content group, and “SeqWins library”.
  • A library of cards: [seqwins_display_library columns="3"] — every SeqWins copied here, including ones you copy later.
  • Widget: “SeqWins”, for sidebars and footers.
  • Paste its link or embed code: a SeqWins’ address from angelsponsoring.com on a line of its own, or its embed code, is drawn here — no frame.

The public library

SeqWins Display → Library → Public library lists the public SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com whose authors share them, with a search, a preview and the codes for each. One you place from there without copying it shows a Show this walkthrough button, and only when a visitor presses it is it loaded inside a frame from angelsponsoring.com. Its viewers are recorded by angelsponsoring.com, not by your website (see External services). Your own SeqWins, copied here, are always drawn and recorded on your website.

Always up to date

  • Instantly: when you edit a SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com, or redact one of its screenshots, your website is told straight away and the copy is refreshed.
  • When viewed: checked in the background, at most every five minutes. Your visitors never wait for it.
  • Twice a day: every copy is checked.
  • Whenever you like: press Refresh now on the SeqWins screen.

Delete or unpublish a SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com and it is removed from your website too. A redacted screenshot’s copies on your website are deleted straight away and never shown again.

Fast by design

  • The title and the whole of step 1 are in the page itself; later steps’ screenshots are fetched as the viewer moves on.
  • One small stylesheet and one small deferred script, only on pages with a SeqWins. A card costs a few kilobytes.
  • Screenshots come from your own website, and a ready-to-show copy of each SeqWins is kept in your object cache or transients.
  • Pages showing a SeqWins can be cached like any other page, and are cleared automatically when it changes, in the common caching plugins.

Your viewers, recorded on your website

Everything a viewer does with a SeqWins copied to your website is recorded on your website, in its own database — not at angelsponsoring.com:

  • Each step reached and ticked off, in order. A step whose link must be opened first waits for it; the last tick can be undone.
  • Signed-in viewers carry on from any device: their progress is kept with their account on your website. A guest who signs in or signs up keeps what they had done.
  • Guests carry on later on their device when they tick Remember my progress on this device (one cookie holding a random code, set only when they tick it). Everybody else is recorded for their visit.
  • Agreement to the terms for using SeqWins, ticked before the first step.
  • Tags from the address they arrive on — …/your-page/#newsletter records “newsletter”.
  • Where people stop: the step most people reach without going further.

Stats and emails

SeqWins Display → Stats shows, for the last 7, 30 or 90 days and for all your SeqWins or one, how many started, finished, opted in, asked for help and followed a link to angelsponsoring.com; a day-by-day chart and table; how far people got through each step; and where they came from. You are emailed about each opt-in, and every morning with a summary of the day before (numbers only, and not on a day with nothing to report); the Dashboard shows the last 7 days and the latest opt-ins. Each email can be switched off, or sent to any address.

Opt-ins and help, kept on your website

When the author asks for a name and email before the steps (an opt-in form, set up with the SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com), the form appears on your website too — with its headline, words and video. What viewers give is kept on your website only: you are emailed about each one, see the latest under SeqWins Display → Tracking & privacy, and can download them all as a CSV file. angelsponsoring.com is told only how many there were.

Each step can also show an Ask for help form. Questions are emailed from your website to you, with the viewer’s email address to reply to, and are not stored on your website or sent to angelsponsoring.com.

Privacy

  • No cookie unless a visitor asks for one by ticking “Remember my progress on this device” (or saying yes to preference cookies on a consent banner that uses the WP Consent API). It holds a random code, and unticking removes it. No IP addresses or anything else that identifies a guest are kept.
  • You choose how long records are kept — 30 days to two years after a viewer’s last visit — and can delete them all at any time. Visits nobody asked to remember are deleted the next day. Both ways of carrying on can be switched off under Tracking & privacy.
  • WordPress’s privacy tools (Tools → Export / Erase Personal Data) include opt-ins and signed-in viewers’ progress, found by email address. Suggested wording for your privacy policy is added under Settings → Privacy.
  • angelsponsoring.com receives no records of people, and the daily totals (numbers per SeqWins per day) only if you switch sharing on.
  • Screenshots come from your website. Visitors’ browsers load nothing from angelsponsoring.com unless you choose to, or they press play on a video, press Show on a public-library SeqWins, or follow a link.
  • The connection key is stored encrypted, and notes from angelsponsoring.com are signed and checked on arrival.
  • Deleting the plugin keeps your data unless you first tick Delete everything when the plugin is deleted.

Referrals and search engines

“Use this SeqWins” links to angelsponsoring.com, at the start and end of each SeqWins, are off until you switch them on under Tracking & privacy. When shown, they carry your account’s referral code, so anyone who signs up there after following one is credited to your account. Step buttons that the author pointed at angelsponsoring.com carry the code too.

Each SeqWins carries HowTo structured data describing its steps. If you switch it on, a page that is nothing but one SeqWins tells search engines the original is on angelsponsoring.com; it is off by default.

Your SeqWins account

SeqWins Display shows the SeqWins in a SeqWins account on angelsponsoring.com, where they are made and stored. Connect the account, and everything described here is part of the plugin.

External services

This plugin relies on Angel Sponsoring (angelsponsoring.com), the service where SeqWins are created and stored, to connect your account and to copy your SeqWins to your website and keep them up to date. The plugin does not contact angelsponsoring.com until you press Connect to SeqWins, or open the Public library tab (which loads the public list from there). SeqWins already copied to your website are shown without contacting it.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you connect: your browser is sent to angelsponsoring.com to sign in and approve. It carries your website’s address and name, the WordPress and plugin versions, the plugin’s name and a one-time security challenge. Your website then sends a one-time code and secret to angelsponsoring.com to complete the connection.
  • Your account’s details — its name, the terms viewers agree to, your referral code and image settings — are received when you connect, and asked for again only when angelsponsoring.com says they have changed, when you press Check now, or to see whether a lost connection is back.
  • When SeqWins are copied or updated: your website sends its connection key and which SeqWins it wants, and receives the SeqWins’ content. Screenshots are downloaded from angelsponsoring.com to your website.
  • To check copies are current (when a SeqWins is viewed, at most every five minutes per SeqWins; and twice a day): your website sends the numbers of the SeqWins it has copied, and receives the current edition of each.
  • Notes from angelsponsoring.com: when you change a SeqWins, angelsponsoring.com sends your website a short signed note saying which SeqWins changed, to /wp-json/seqwins-display/v1/notify on your website. It contains no personal data. Your website then asks angelsponsoring.com for the change itself.
  • When you disconnect, switch the plugin off (unless you untick that under Tracking & privacy), or delete the plugin with “Delete everything” ticked: your website tells angelsponsoring.com, so your account no longer lists it.
  • Daily totals, only if you switch sharing on (Tracking & privacy; off by default): once a day your website sends, for each SeqWins and day, how many viewers started, finished, reached each step, opted in, followed a link to angelsponsoring.com, or asked for help. Numbers only.
  • With every request after connecting, your website sends its connection key, its address and name, the WordPress and plugin versions, the plugin’s name, and its address for notes.
  • When you press “Create a SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com”: your browser opens the SeqWins builder there, with your website’s connection number so it can offer the way back.

What visitors’ browsers load from elsewhere, and when:

  • Screenshots are shown from the copies on your website. Only if you choose to serve screenshots from angelsponsoring.com (Tracking & privacy; off by default) are they loaded from angelsponsoring.com or its content delivery network, which then receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details.
  • A public-library SeqWins you place without copying it is loaded inside a frame from angelsponsoring.com when the visitor presses Show (or, if you switch that on, as it comes into view). angelsponsoring.com then receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details and records that viewer’s progress itself.
  • A video in a SeqWins is loaded only when the visitor presses play: from angelsponsoring.com, or from YouTube, Vimeo or Rumble when the author chose a video there. That service then receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details.
  • Links and buttons take the visitor to the address they show; links to angelsponsoring.com carry your account’s referral code.

The services and their terms:

  • Angel Sponsoring (angelsponsoring.com), provided by Destiny Express Ltd: Terms and conditions · Privacy policy
  • YouTube (youtube-nocookie.com), provided by Google: Terms of service · Privacy policy
  • Vimeo (player.vimeo.com), provided by Vimeo.com, Inc.: Terms of service · Privacy policy
  • Rumble (rumble.com), provided by Rumble Inc.: Terms and conditions · Privacy policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to SeqWins Display in wp-admin and press Connect to SeqWins.
  3. Sign in to angelsponsoring.com, approve your website, and choose your SeqWins.

Your website needs to be able to make outgoing HTTPS requests, as nearly all hosts allow.

For testing against a staging copy of angelsponsoring.com, add define( 'SEQWINS_DISPLAY_SOURCE', 'https://staging…' ); to wp-config.php.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account on angelsponsoring.com?

Yes. SeqWins are made and stored there, and the plugin shows the ones in your account.

Can more than one account be connected to a website?

No. Each website connects to one SeqWins account, chosen by whoever manages the website.

I approved the connection but was not brought back.

The approval page shows a connection code. Open SeqWins Display on your website, choose “Enter the code instead”, and type it in. It works once, within ten minutes.

It says this site’s security keys have changed.

Some security plugins change the keys in wp-config.php, and the saved connection is encrypted with them. Press Connect to SeqWins again. Your copied SeqWins are kept, and shown meanwhile.

How is the connection kept secure?

  • Connecting uses a one-time code that only works together with a secret your website never sends anywhere, so it is useless to anybody who sees it.
  • The connection key is stored encrypted in your database (libsodium, or OpenSSL AES-256-GCM), with a key made from your site’s own security keys in wp-config.php. It can only read your own account’s details and SeqWins, and can be disconnected at any time, from your website or from your account on angelsponsoring.com.
  • Notes from angelsponsoring.com are signed (HMAC-SHA256 with your connection’s key) and checked on arrival. Notes that are unsigned, wrongly signed, more than five minutes old or already received are refused.
  • Visitors’ requests to /wp-json/seqwins-display/v1/viewer can only record that visitor’s own progress, opt-in or help request on a SeqWins copied here, are limited in number, are never cached, and store no IP addresses.
  • Every form and button in wp-admin checks a nonce and that you may manage the site.

What happens to my copies if angelsponsoring.com is down, or I disconnect?

They are shown as usual. Your website checks its copies twice a day; if a check fails it tries again over the next hour, and while it can’t get through, copying and refreshing wait, with a message in wp-admin saying why. They carry on by themselves once the connection returns (or once you connect again).

My website is behind a firewall. Will updates still arrive?

Yes. The instant notes may not get through, but copies are still checked when viewed and twice a day, and you can press Refresh now at any time.

What happens when I redact a screenshot?

The pictures copied to your website are deleted straight away and never shown again. Its steps keep showing, with “This picture is being updated” where each screenshot was, until the new pictures arrive — even on pages your visitors already have open.

Which editors can I place a SeqWins with?

  • Block editor: the “SeqWins” block in the Embeds group, with “Show: the whole SeqWins / its card”.
  • Shortcodes work in the classic editor, Shortcode blocks and text widgets.
  • WPBakery: a “SeqWins” element in the Content group (whole or card), and “SeqWins library”.
  • Embed code from angelsponsoring.com works in either form (card or whole).
  • The public library gives a block, shortcode, WPBakery code and HTML for each SeqWins it lists.

Where is viewers’ progress kept?

For every SeqWins copied to your website: in your website’s own database, in four tables — wp_simplet_display_progress (each visit’s steps), wp_simplet_display_viewers (when they were seen, their tags and terms agreement), wp_simplet_display_leads (opt-ins) and wp_simplet_display_counts (daily totals, numbers only). They are removed when the plugin is deleted with “Delete everything” ticked.

So that nobody can fill your database by sending made-up progress, each visit can record only so much: about six changes per step of a SeqWins an hour, plus 30 to spare, and your website starts recording at most 120 new visits a minute. Past either limit the SeqWins carries on working on the page; that visit’s progress just isn’t recorded.

Can I make or edit a SeqWins in WordPress?

No. SeqWins are made and edited on angelsponsoring.com. The plugin takes you there with one button, and shows, records and reports on what you make.

Where do opt-ins go?

Into your website’s own database (wp_simplet_display_leads), and an email to you for each one, with who, which SeqWins and which page. They are included in WordPress’s export and erase tools by email address, and are not sent to angelsponsoring.com. A mailing-list plugin on your website can pick them up through the seqwins_display_lead_captured action.

Does it set cookies?

Only when a visitor asks: ticking Remember my progress on this device sets sd_viewer (a random code, HttpOnly) and sd_consent, for your retention period. Unticking removes them. Signed-in viewers need no cookie of ours: their progress is kept with their account. Consent banners that use the WP Consent API are told about the cookie, and a yes to preference cookies there counts as ticking the box. You can switch the box off under Tracking & privacy.

Where are the screenshots kept?

In a folder inside your website’s uploads folder (usually wp-content/uploads/simplet-display/), one folder per SeqWins, not in your Media Library. They are deleted when you remove a SeqWins from your website, or delete the plugin with “Delete everything” ticked. You can choose to serve them from angelsponsoring.com instead, under Tracking & privacy; this website’s copies are then used if angelsponsoring.com cannot be reached.

I deleted the plugin. Is my data gone?

Not unless you ticked Delete everything when the plugin is deleted (under SeqWins Display → Tracking & privacy) first. By default, deleting the plugin keeps your copied SeqWins, opt-ins, stats and settings, so reinstalling it and pressing Connect brings everything back. Switching the plugin off (which deleting does first) disconnects it from your SeqWins account, unless you untick Disconnect from angelsponsoring.com when the plugin is switched off.

Will it slow my pages down, or upset my caching plugin?

No. Pages without a SeqWins carry nothing from it. Pages showing a SeqWins can be cached like any other page: they are the same for every visitor who is not signed in, and set no cookie when viewed. Each visitor’s progress goes to your website separately, as a request no cache keeps.

  • Cached pages showing a SeqWins are cleared automatically when it changes in WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP-Optimize and SiteGround Speed Optimizer. Other caches can listen for the seqwins_display_purge_post action.
  • The small viewer script is kept out of “delay JavaScript”, combining and minifying (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, SiteGround Speed Optimizer, Autoptimize, Cloudflare Rocket Loader), so the first press of a button always works.
  • SeqWins Display → Cache tools shows what is kept and which caching plugins were found, with buttons to check or refresh every copy, copy the screenshots again, clear the fast copies, or clear cached pages.
sections.changelog:
3.3.2

  • Viewers’ pages and the privacy tools say “SeqWins” directly, with nothing in between.
  • Requests to angelsponsoring.com name the plugin and nothing else about it.
  • Keeps less of angelsponsoring.com’s answer: what the plugin does not use is no longer stored.

3.3.1

  • As planned for 3.3: SeqWins Display names itself in every request, and angelsponsoring.com answers with the plugin’s whole service for any connected account.
  • Viewers carry on later, on every site: signed-in viewers from any device, and guests on their device when they tick “Remember my progress on this device”. Both on, and each can be switched off under Tracking & privacy.
  • As planned: every action and filter is named seqwins_display_….
  • Errors SeqWins Display reports are its own; other plugins and themes report theirs.
  • Fixed: a SeqWins copied to your website could fail to appear on its page.
  • Fixed: the SeqWins screen could fail to open once connected, and the Check, Refresh and Copy again buttons under Cache tools could fail.

3.2.1

  • A public-library SeqWins placed without copying it shows a “Show this walkthrough” button, and loads from angelsponsoring.com only when it is pressed (unless you choose otherwise under Tracking & privacy).
  • Your account’s details arrive when you connect, and are asked for again only when angelsponsoring.com says they changed or you press Check now.
  • Each visit can record only so much progress, so the visitors’ address can’t be used to fill your database.
  • Adds license.txt (GPLv2 or later).

  • To check copies are current (when a SeqWins is viewed, at most every five minutes per SeqWins; and twice a day): your website sends the numbers of the SeqWins it has copied, and receives the current edition of each.
  • Notes from angelsponsoring.com: when you change a SeqWins, angelsponsoring.com sends your website a short signed note saying which SeqWins changed, to /wp-json/seqwins-display/v1/notify on your website. It contains no personal data. Your website then asks angelsponsoring.com for the change itself.
  • When you disconnect, switch the plugin off (unless you untick that under Tracking & privacy), or delete the plugin with “Delete everything” ticked: your website tells angelsponsoring.com, so your account no longer lists it.
  • Daily totals, only if you switch sharing on (Tracking & privacy; off by default): once a day your website sends, for each SeqWins and day, how many viewers started, finished, reached each step, opted in, followed a link to angelsponsoring.com, or asked for help. Numbers only.
  • With every request after connecting, your website sends its connection key, its address and name, the WordPress and plugin versions, the plugin’s name, and its address for notes.
  • When you press “Create a SeqWins on angelsponsoring.com”: your browser opens the SeqWins builder there, with your website’s connection number so it can offer the way back.

What visitors’ browsers load from elsewhere, and when:

  • Screenshots are shown from the copies on your website. Only if you choose to serve screenshots from angelsponsoring.com (Tracking & privacy; off by default) are they loaded from angelsponsoring.com or its content delivery network, which then receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details.
  • A public-library SeqWins you place without copying it is loaded inside a frame from angelsponsoring.com when the visitor presses Show (or, if you switch that on, as it comes into view). angelsponsoring.com then receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details and records that viewer’s progress itself.
  • A video in a SeqWins is loaded only when the visitor presses play: from angelsponsoring.com, or from YouTube, Vimeo or Rumble when the author chose a video there. That service then receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details.
  • Links and buttons take the visitor to the address they show; links to angelsponsoring.com carry your account’s referral code.
